subject: S-X2 p-values in mirt: are they corrected for Type 1 error rates?

messages.author: c1f40f19e0a4bab0
messages.subject: S-X2 p-values in mirt: are they corrected for Type 1 error rates?
parts:
In a paper I was reading, it said they used the polytomous extension of S-X2 and identified some items as misfitting at p < 0.05 "after controlling for Type I error rates with the Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment". 

1.  Are the p-values reported by mirt's "itemfit" function adjusted in this way already?  
2. Is p<0.05 the usual criterion?  I read at least 2 other papers that use p< 0.01 as the criterion for misfit identification.

Thanks

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: S-X2 p-values in mirt: are they corrected for Type 1 error rates?
parts:
On Sun, Apr 1, 2018 at 9:35 PM, Joe Le Doux <ledou...@gmail.com> wrote:
In a paper I was reading, it said they used the polytomous extension of S-X2 and identified some items as misfitting at p < 0.05 "after controlling for Type I error rates with the Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment". 

1.  Are the p-values reported by mirt's "itemfit" function adjusted in this way already?
No, they are interpreted as-is. You are free of course to adjust these by simply extracting the p-values from the returned object and passing them to p.adjust() to apply a FWE correction.
2. Is p<0.05 the usual criterion?  I read at least 2 other papers that use p< 0.01 as the criterion for misfit identification.

Matter of convention. It's basically the same question as asking "should my independent t-test use alpha = .05 or .01?". It depends on how often you are willing to make a Type I error. HTH.
 

Thanks
